newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes Kenyan government announcements.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes Kenyan government announcements.

text.p: The United States welcomes the Kenyan government's plan to engage in dialogue with the opposition and to implement political reforms before national elections, the U.S. State Department said on Friday.

"The responsibility for the success of this process rests with both sides. Government and the opposition must engage in this dialogue in the democratic spirit of compromise and with the best interest of the Kenyan people foremost in mind," State Department deputy spokesman James Foley said.
In a statement, he said it was also essential that pre-election rallies and other events remained peaceful.
During the past two months there have been numerous clashes between riot police and demonstrators demanding political reforms.

Earlier on Friday, Kenya's government announced that an opposition-backed rally in the Indian Ocean city of Mombasa would be permitted, greatly reducing the chances of new clashes between police and demonstrators.
The reforms demanded by the opposition would cut the power of President Daniel arap Moi, who has been in power for 19 years. No date has been set for presidential and parliamentary polls this year.
